title: BE CAREFUL! they are scammers
body: Horrible: an app that is supposedly promoting well-being and they’re scamming people out of their money. I downloaded this, never getting a paid subscription and deleted the same day after checking it out and deciding it had nothing to offer me. I just noticed they billed me a 100 € (57 for some bundle and 40 for a separate application). I never knowingly agreed to any paid subscription and when I went to cancel the scam continued. Everyone knows how there’s often intentional complications made in the cancellation process to trick people to stay. With this one they did the following manipulative bs: asking if you’re sure about cancelling multiple times, phrasing the question differently, switching the placement of the yes and no buttons, boldly highlighting the answer that makes you agree to a pause instead of a cancellation, using complicated sentence structures that you have to keep checking like it is a literary test; and making the cancellation confirming answers hard to read or even notice by making the font small and thinned out and hiding it further away from the rest of the options. This is doubly messed up considering this is an app sought after by many neurodivergent people like myself who struggle with focus even without such manipulations. I cannot even imagine how tough it might be for anyone dyslexic to manage to get through that cancellation process! So please watch out for yourselves people!

title: extremely confusing and feels like a complete waste of money
body:
This app is extremely confusing and is a complete waste of money. The monthly price is unreasonably(!!!!!!) high! For those of us with ADHD, be sure to cancel the free trial if it doesn’t meet your needs—I forgot, as I often do. I made the cancellation on 14th day (last day of the trial) and was still charged 39,99€.  To make matters worse, they’ve made the cancellation process unnecessarily difficult which seems really convenient for them, not so convenient for the people with ADHD. This seems like a they’re taking purposly advantage of people with ADHD. 

So this is how it goes: Download this app to get a better grip on your life and manage your ADHD—only to find yourself confused, procrastinating, and stuck with a tricky cancellation process until the last moment. You’ll likely lose €39.99 and be left feeling disappointed in yourself and worse than before the trial. Great job.

title: Good app but with issues
body: I found the app helpful and motivating in sustaining habits such as drinking water, yoga etc.  The app is functional, however, there are some windows or functions that can be closed only after some time, e.g. after an animation or message, which can be frustrating in the long run. Also, what I find disturbing, is that the habits and challenges promote behaviors that are questionable for physical and mental health. I especially talk here about the promoted habit of checking the weight every day (pointless for weight loss and may be damaging to self esteem), intermittent fasting (questionable for long term weight loss), exercising every day (what about recovery and rest days?) and stretching without warmup (can be damaging to muscles). I recommend checking some of the habits twice with some more reliable sport, nutrition and health related research and expert opinions.

I suffer from ADD and was hoping this app could help me with routines, but I don’t need an app to remind me to drink water in the morning. There is only one explanation for this, the makers of the app doesn't think that the customers will keep their subscription if they don't pay for the whole year.
